Genesis 1:3 • Hebrew Word Study

Let There Be Light

אוֹר
Or
light
“And God said, Let there be light: and there was light.”
← Back to Bible Study

Follow the Word

GENESIS 1:3
God speaks light into being.

EXODUS 10:23
Israel has light in the darkness.

PSALM 27:1
The LORD is my light.

JOHN 8:12
Jesus: “I am the light of the world.”

REVELATION 21:23
The glory of God gives the city light.

Faith & Application

Darkness never gets the final word.

The Hebrew word for “light” is אוֹר (or).

Light is mentioned in Genesis 1:3:

“And God said, Let there be light: and there was light.”

On that day, He divided the light from the darkness and called them day and night.

But what was this light?

There was no luminary to produce it. By luminary, I’m referring to something that gives or bears light…the sun, moon, stars, an oil lamp, fire. Nothing. So what was this light?

God didn’t make what we would call the natural luminaries, the sun, moon, and stars, until Day Four. Before we ever got the sun, moon, and stars, God had already caused dry land to appear and had brought forth grass, herbs, and fruit trees.

I guess God had to flip on a light before He could create the rest.

I wonder if we still see some evidence of that original light and simply don’t know it. Does it have a certain hue to it? What exactly was it?

From what I understand, the Hebrew word אוֹר (or) does not, by itself, mean some special “God-like” or divine light. It is the ordinary Hebrew word for light, and it is used in several other places in the Bible.

Light in the Midst of Darkness

We see אוֹר (or) again with the children of Israel in their dealings with Pharaoh. God caused a thick darkness to fall over Egypt. For three days, the Egyptians could not see one another or leave their places, “but all the children of Israel had light in their dwellings” (Exodus 10:23).

That “light” is אוֹר (or).

I think that is fascinating. God provided light for His people in the midst of darkness, distinguishing them from Egypt and reminding them that they were His.

God continued to provide light for them after they left Egypt. As they traveled, He went before them in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night, “to give them light” so that they could travel day and night (Exodus 13:21).

FOLLOW THE LIGHT
Psalm 27:1 — “The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear?”
Psalm 43:3 — “O send out thy light and thy truth: let them lead me.”
Psalm 119:105 — “Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.”
Isaiah 60:19 — “The LORD shall be unto thee an everlasting light.”

When everything else is dark, God is light.

Jesus said in John 8:12:

“I am the light of the world: he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life.”

I think sometimes we become convinced of the overshadowing darkness and despair around us. But over and over, God spells it out for us, even from the beginning:

“Let there be light: and there was light.”

It wasn’t the sun, moon, or stars. Those had not been created yet. Scripture doesn’t tell us exactly what produced that first light. Could it somehow have been associated with God’s own presence and glory? We do know this: God spoke, and there was light.

From Genesis to Revelation

And there will come another time when there will be a new heaven and a new earth. Revelation 21:23 says:

“And the city had no need of the sun, neither of the moon, to shine in it: for the glory of God did lighten it, and the Lamb is the light thereof.”

You see, things are going to end in much the same way as they began:

with no need for the sun or moon to provide the light, and with the presence and glory of God lighting everything.

From “Let there be light” in Genesis to “the glory of God did lighten it” in Revelation, darkness never gets the final word.

HIS WORD • HIS COVENANT • HIS KINGDOM
It all started with His Word.
